item.title: Protecting Human Rights at the World Cup: Progress on Paper, Gaps on the Ground
item.description: As the 2026 World Cup draws to a close, this article examines FIFA’s evolving commitments to human rights, its record at recent tournaments, and factors that will determine whether protections for workers, fans, and players improve, stall, or decline at future tournaments.

item.title: Playbook or Rental? U.S. Counter-Drone Defense and the 2026 World Cup
item.description: For the 2026 World Cup, the United States built its first nationwide drone defense in months. Whether the country keeps a counter-drone playbook it can carry forward, or returns a six-week rental once the stadiums empty, is the choice it faces the morning after the final.

item.title: The NATO Ankara Summit: Delivery over Drama
item.description: The NATO Ankara Summit may have lacked dramatic headlines, but it delivered where it mattered most—advancing European defense capabilities, reinforcing support for Ukraine, and demonstrating that Alliance adaptation continues amid strategic uncertainty.

item.title: What the Iran War Is Costing Joint Gulf-U.S. Ambitions for AI
item.description: For decades, Gulf states invested trillions into the U.S. economy, tied their security to Washington, and bet that alignment was the price of protection. The Iran war raised a clear question: Was alignment the cause of the threat, rather than the cure for it?

item.title: States Weekly Newsletter: July 15, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers July 15, 2026.

item.title: Beyond Oil: Vision 2030 at Ten
item.description: This installment of Charting the Middle East explores the progress Saudi Arabia has made in diversifying its economy 10 years after the launch of Vision 2030.

item.title: Reflections from URC 2026: Ukraine’s Reconstruction Has Become Wartime Resilience
item.description: The Ukraine Recovery Conference is now a platform that supports Ukraine’s strategic industries and infrastructure, and embeds Ukraine deeper into European security architecture. The most noticeable outcome of this year’s conference is a shift toward wartime resilience.

item.title: The Hormuz Energy Crisis Generates a Tailwind for Nuclear Energy in Northeast Asia
item.description: The Hormuz energy crisis has constrained the global supply of LNG and elevated LNG prices. How is the crisis shaping the role of nuclear energy in Northeast Asian economies that have high LNG import dependence?

item.title: Understanding Russia-Iran Collaboration in Cyberspace
item.description: Cyber collaboration between Russia and Iran in the U.S.-Iran conflict has been overstated based on currently cited evidence. While cross-border cyber cooperation is happening in some areas, the Russia-Iran cyber reality is much thornier and much trickier to interpret than some headlines suggest.
